findings_and_repairs.finding: A global cue/ring color swap preserved selected payload positions and was not a causal crossed control.
findings_and_repairs.repair: Swap only the true interior cue cell and ring decoy cell while holding remote payload positions and counts fixed.

findings_and_repairs.finding: The minimum lesson could otherwise admit a seed-dependent fixed-color shortcut.
findings_and_repairs.repair: First two demonstrations use different cue colors and jointly cover all six decor colors in crossed semantic roles.

findings_and_repairs.finding: A payload could occupy an expanded-selector corner before the intended ring decoy and make the wrong intermediate recover the true cue.
findings_and_repairs.repair: Reserve the complete one-cell-expanded selector zone from payload placement.

findings_and_repairs.finding: A cue-colored crosshair nuisance could appear inside the expanded selector before the ring decoy.
findings_and_repairs.repair: Keep every crosshair nuisance outside the complete one-cell-expanded selector zone.

limits: Finite bounded attacks do not prove universal uniqueness. Owner source review, native qualification/acceptance, and training admission remain separate.
